chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is upon you with the restraint and neglect of the immoralities'.

key_terms.الْعَفَافِ: Self-restraint, chastity, or moderation in desires and actions
key_terms.الْفُجُورِ: Immorality, extravagance, or deviation from righteousness

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) say about self-restraint and avoiding immorality?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith links the Prophet’s command for self-restraint (al-'iffah) and avoiding immorality (al-fujur) to the reciprocal divine protection of one’s own sanctity. It underscores the Shia principle that ethical purity in dealings with others ensures one’s own dignity and spiritual security are preserved by Allah.
